title: Shared drying and cooling pods for farmer groups
problem: Small and marginal farmers (86% of landholders) lose income when produce spoils or is rejected, because storage, drying and cooling are out of reach.
solution: Low-cost solar dryer and cooling pods placed at farmer-group sites and rented per batch.

roles.elec: Solar supply, fans and moisture sensors

model.revenue: Rent per batch plus yearly group plan

checks.demand: Post-harvest losses are estimated at 68.9 million tonnes a year.
checks.today: Sell fast at low price or lose the crop.
checks.who: Vegetable and fruit growers in groups of 20+.
checks.wedge: One dryer pod rented by one FPO for one season.
checks.seen: Visit 15 farmers and record what they lose each month.
checks.future: Heat and unstable weather keep raising spoilage risk.

evidence.title: RESET 2026: dialogues to reduce food loss and waste in India (WRI India)
RESET 2026 background note (WRI India)

title: Invoice tracker and polite reminder tool for small suppliers
problem: Small businesses wait about 73 days on average to be paid, which locks up cash they need to run the business.
solution: App that tracks invoices, sends polite reminders and prepares the paperwork for the MSME dispute process.

checks.demand: Thousands of crores in dues are pending and many cases are over a year old.
checks.today: Phone calls, WhatsApp and Excel sheets.
checks.who: Small manufacturers selling to larger buyers.
checks.wedge: Invoice tracking and reminders for 20 shops.
checks.seen: Interview 15 suppliers about their last late payment.
checks.future: A new law adds time limits, so tools that follow them will be needed.

evidence.title: Indian MSMEs face mounting delayed payments: Recordent report (Telangana Today)
MSME bill could be an IBC moment for delayed payments (Tribune, CRISIL)

title: Street-level flood alerts from low-cost drain sensors
problem: Blocked drains turn short heavy rain into street flooding, and residents get no warning of which roads will go under.
solution: Cheap water-level sensors in key drains feed a map that warns residents and the ward office.

checks.demand: Cities such as Mumbai, Chennai and Bengaluru flood repeatedly.
checks.today: Wait and check social media.
checks.wedge: Five sensors and a text alert for one colony.
checks.seen: Walk one flood-prone street and ask 20 residents.
checks.future: Heavier rain events are expected to be more frequent.

evidence.title: Urban flooding in India: causes, consequences and solutions (Drishti IAS)
Urban flooding in India (Vajiram)

title: Safe e-waste pickup and payment for households
problem: About 95% of e-waste goes to informal recyclers who burn and acid-soak parts, harming workers, while households get little for old devices.
solution: Pickup service that pays a fair price and hands devices to authorised recyclers with a receipt.

model.revenue: Margin on resale and recycler fees

checks.demand: Formal collection and recycling capacity is thin.
checks.today: Sell to a local scrap dealer or keep it at home.
checks.who: Residents of apartment societies and small offices.
checks.wedge: Pickup from three housing societies once a month.
checks.seen: Ask 30 households what they did with their last old phone.
checks.future: E-waste volumes keep growing each year.

evidence.title: How e-waste crisis continues to plague informal sector (Down To Earth)

title: Village health kiosk with a booked specialist video call
problem: A rural Community Health Centre has about 80% fewer specialists than sanctioned, and one Primary Health Centre serves over 36,000 people.
solution: Trained local operator runs a kiosk with basic vitals devices and booked video consults with specialists.

model.revenue: Fee per consult plus operator share

checks.demand: Specialist posts in rural centres stay vacant.
checks.today: Travel to a town and lose a day's wages.
checks.who: Families in villages far from district hospitals.
checks.wedge: One kiosk offering two specialist slots a week.
checks.seen: Talk to 20 villagers about their last trip for care.
checks.future: Demand for tele-consults keeps growing.

evidence.title: We don't have enough doctors in rural India, that's why we need telemedicine (BW Disrupt)
Is telemedicine filling the gap in tier 2 and 3 cities (BioSpectrum)

title: Skill proof portfolios for polytechnic and ITI students
problem: Polytechnic and ITI graduates have low employability scores, and employers cannot easily see what they can actually do.
solution: App where students log real projects and get them checked by mentors, giving employers a proof-based profile.

model.revenue: Per-student college plan and employer listing fee

checks.demand: Employability gaps are widest for ITI and polytechnic streams.
checks.today: CV with marks only.
checks.who: Final-year diploma students in small towns.
checks.wedge: Portfolio pages for one college batch.
checks.seen: Ask five placement officers what proof employers want.
checks.future: Skills-based hiring keeps growing.

evidence.title: India Skills Report 2026 (Careers360)
Employability skills and the India job crisis (National Skills Network)

title: Indoor air checks and fixes for homes and schools
problem: Indoor air in Indian homes can be two to five times more polluted than outdoor air, yet people only watch outdoor AQI.
solution: Low-cost indoor monitor plus a simple report that suggests cheap fixes like ventilation and cooking changes.

model.customer: Schools and families in polluted cities

checks.demand: People already buy purifiers without knowing their indoor air.
checks.today: Check outdoor AQI apps or buy a purifier blindly.
checks.who: Parents of children and elderly residents.
checks.wedge: Rent a monitor for a week to ten homes.
checks.seen: Measure the air in ten homes and share results.
checks.future: Pollution seasons are getting longer.

evidence.title: Jan 29, 2026: air quality is 'very poor' even in south Delhi homes (Newslaundry)
Why indoor air pollution must be on India's health agenda (Ahmedabad University)

title: Solar sizing and payback helper for small factories
problem: Small high-power businesses worry about solar performance and know little about it, so many keep paying high power bills.
solution: Tool that reads a bill, sizes a rooftop system, compares installers and shows real payback.

checks.demand: Surveys show low awareness and perceived risk among small firms.
checks.today: Rely on one installer's pitch.
checks.who: Workshop owners with large power bills.
checks.wedge: A bill-to-payback report for 30 workshops.
checks.seen: Ask ten owners why they have not installed solar.
checks.future: Rooftop capacity is growing quickly.

evidence.title: Solar mission faces challenge from high-power small businesses (India Environment Portal)
Reasons preventing faster rooftop solar adoption in India (SolarSquare)

title: Cool rest and water points for delivery riders
problem: Delivery workers ride through afternoon heat with no shade, water or toilets, and cannot stop without losing pay.
solution: Shaded rest points with chilled water and charging near busy pickup spots, paid for by platforms and shops.

roles.biz: Sponsor deals with shops and platforms

checks.demand: Heat stress is now routine among delivery workers.
checks.today: Rest on pavements and buy water from shops.
checks.wedge: One rest point near a busy food street.
checks.seen: Spend an afternoon with ten riders.
checks.future: Heatwaves are expected to increase.

evidence.title: Piping hot: India's delivery economy runs on worker heat stress (Newslaundry)
Heatwave warnings but no relief: gig workers push for protections (The South First)

title: Daily check-in and helper network for seniors living alone
problem: About half of India's seniors report loneliness, and many live far from children who have migrated for work.
solution: Daily check-in calls, local helper visits for small tasks, and alerts to family if there is no response.

checks.demand: The senior population is growing fast and care services are thin.
checks.today: Phone calls when family remembers.
checks.wedge: Daily call and two helper visits a month for 20 families.
checks.seen: Interview 15 families about how they check on parents.
checks.future: The senior population keeps growing.

evidence.title: India is facing a silent elderly care crisis (NCAER)
Empty courtyards, fading voices: elderly isolation amid migration (Exchange4media)

title: Construction waste blocks and tiles for low-cost homes
problem: Building costs rose about 40% in five years, while construction waste is dumped in huge volumes, leaving affordable homes out of reach.
solution: Small machines that turn site waste into bricks and paver blocks sold back to builders and masons.

model.revenue: Block sales plus waste pickup fee

checks.demand: Cement, steel and labour costs keep climbing.
checks.today: Buy new material and pay to dump waste.
checks.who: Small contractors on repair and low-rise jobs.
checks.wedge: Paver blocks from waste of one nearby site.
checks.seen: Ask ten contractors what they pay to dump waste.
checks.future: Waste and costs both keep rising.

evidence.title: Construction costs in India surge 40% in five years (NBM&CW)
Re-Build India: converting construction waste into affordable shelter (SJP journal)

title: Scam check helper for seniors and first-time UPI users
problem: Cyber fraud complaints crossed 12.7 lakh in the first half of 2026, and seniors are often the targets of UPI and phone scams.
solution: Simple app and WhatsApp bot where users paste a message or number and get a plain-language risk check.

roles.biz: Bank, society and senior group tie-ups

checks.demand: Losses from cyber fraud run to thousands of crores.
checks.today: Ask a relative or ignore calls.
checks.wedge: A WhatsApp checker for the top ten scam types.
checks.seen: Collect 50 real scam messages from relatives.
checks.future: Digital payments keep growing.

evidence.title: WEF calls cyber fraud 'pervasive' as India faces rising scam losses (The Quint)
India reports ₹805 crore UPI fraud till Nov FY26 (Free Press Journal)

title: Credit book and restocking tool for kirana stores
problem: Neighbourhood grocery stores track customer credit on paper and get little supplier credit, which strains cash and stock.
solution: Phone app for customer credit, reminders and restock suggestions, with supplier offers.

model.value: Better cash and less lost credit
model.revenue: Small monthly plan plus supplier fees

checks.demand: Around 90% of grocery trade runs through small stores.
checks.today: Notebook of credit and phone calls to suppliers.
checks.wedge: Credit book and reminders for 30 shops.
checks.seen: Sit in five shops for a day and watch.
checks.future: Retail keeps digitising.

evidence.title: Digitising Indian retail: challenges and growth models (ORF)
How kirana stores can reduce payment failures (Innoviti)

title: Drip kits and soil-moisture alerts for depleted-borewell farms
problem: Groundwater supplies 62% of irrigation, and deeper wells in depleted areas often give brackish or unreliable water.
solution: Low-cost drip kit with a soil-moisture sensor that texts the farmer when watering is actually needed.

roles.elec: Moisture sensor and solar pump timer

model.revenue: Kit sale plus yearly alert plan

checks.demand: Water tables keep falling in many states.
checks.today: Run the pump on a fixed schedule.
checks.wedge: Sensors and alerts for ten plots.
checks.seen: Join farmers for a watering round.
checks.future: Groundwater loss is projected to speed up.

evidence.title: When wells fail: farmers' response to groundwater depletion in India (IFPRI)
India will be losing groundwater three times faster in 2041-2080 (Down To Earth)

title: Peer support and career guidance for exam students
problem: Many students do not know where to get mental-health help in school, and nearly half have never had structured career counselling.
solution: App with trained peer mentors, anonymous check-ins, and a path to Tele-MANAS and local counsellors.

model.value: Early help and clear next steps

checks.demand: Surveys report many students rarely feel calm or motivated.
checks.today: Cope alone or tell a friend.
checks.wedge: Anonymous check-ins and referrals for one hostel.
checks.seen: Ask 20 students where they would go for help.
checks.future: Exam competition is growing.

evidence.title: Rising student deaths by suicide: what the 2024 NCRB report shows (The Wire)
One in five students rarely feels calm: IC3 report (Free Press Journal)

title: Source segregation tracker for housing societies
problem: Only 30–35% of municipal waste is segregated, and even Bengaluru's source segregation has stalled near 54%.
solution: Society app that tracks bin-level segregation, gives feedback to flats and reports for the new waste rules.

checks.demand: New solid waste rules ask for stronger segregation and tracking.
checks.today: Reminders on notice boards.
checks.wedge: Photo checks and a weekly score for one society.
checks.seen: Join a pickup round in one society.
checks.future: Rules and fees keep getting stricter.

evidence.title: Once pioneer in garbage segregation, Bengaluru struggles to regain momentum (Deccan Herald)
Solid Waste Management Rules, 2026: implementation readiness (IMPRI)

title: Affordable helmet rental and safety kit for bike taxi and delivery riders
problem: About 73% of two-wheeler riders who died in 2023 were not wearing a helmet, and two-wheelers account for 45% of road deaths.
solution: Quality helmets with a lockable carrier on rent or low monthly instalments for working riders.

model.value: Safer rides at low upfront cost

checks.demand: Most deaths among riders involve no helmet.
checks.today: Skip it or buy a cheap one.
checks.wedge: One rental stand with 30 helmets near a hub.
checks.seen: Count helmet use at one junction for a day.
checks.future: Two-wheeler use keeps growing.

evidence.title: More two-wheelers, gig workers under pressure: 9 bike riders die every hour (Newslaundry)
Indian roads are deadliest for pedestrians, two-wheeler riders (Scroll)

title: Direct online store and design help for weavers
problem: Nearly two-thirds of handloom weavers earn under ₹5,000 a month and depend on middlemen, with almost no e-commerce use.
solution: Marketplace that photographs, lists and ships weaver products with fair price splits and design guidance.

checks.demand: Artisans have little control over pricing or direct sales.
checks.today: Sell to a master weaver or at a fair stall.
checks.wedge: Ten weavers' products listed in one store.
checks.seen: Visit one cluster and learn how orders flow.
checks.future: Demand for handmade goods keeps growing.

evidence.title: Bandhej, Ikkat and Zari are everywhere, but India's artisans are struggling (The Week)
India saved handloom. Now it must save weaving as a livelihood (YourStory)

title: Milk quality test and health alert for small dairy farmers
problem: Small dairy farmers with one or two animals face cattle disease, poor feed and unsafe raw milk, and only about 20% of milk reaches organised markets.
solution: Handheld milk tester at collection points with a phone log that flags quality and sick-animal patterns.

model.value: Fair pay for quality, early disease alerts

checks.demand: Diseases like lumpy skin disease cut milk output by 20 to 50%.
checks.today: Judge quality by eye and smell.
checks.who: Dairy societies collecting from small herds.
checks.wedge: One tester at one collection point for a month.
checks.seen: Visit a collection centre and watch the morning rush.
checks.future: Disease and feed pressure keep growing.

evidence.title: Challenges in intensifying India smallholder dairy production (ILRI)

title: Battery health check and second-life packs for e-rickshaw owners
problem: EV battery waste is growing, and much of it ends up in informal recycling or is exported as black mass, losing valuable materials.
solution: Test used batteries, resell good ones for solar backup and send the rest to authorised recyclers.

model.customer: E-rickshaw owners and shops needing backup

checks.demand: EV numbers rose forty-fold since 2016.
checks.today: Sell to scrap dealers.
checks.wedge: Test and buy back batteries from one stand.
checks.seen: Ask 15 owners how they dispose of weak batteries.
checks.future: More EVs mean more used batteries each year.

evidence.title: Is there a future for re-using EV batteries in India (Oxford Smith School)
Can India's battery recycling ecosystem keep pace with EV growth (Autocar Pro)

title: Ice and cold box service for small fishers
problem: Post-harvest fish losses are estimated at 15–30% because small fishers lack ice, storage and cold transport.
solution: Insulated boxes and small ice supply at landing sites, rented per trip with a simple order app.

roles.elec: Solar ice maker and temperature logger

checks.demand: Poor cold chains reduce fisher income.
checks.today: Sell immediately at any price.
checks.wedge: Rent ten boxes at one landing site.
checks.seen: Stand at a landing site for two mornings.
checks.future: Cold chains will matter more as catches vary.

evidence.title: Post-harvest losses in fisheries: a barrier to export growth (IMPRI)
Blue revolution and small-scale fishers (The Wire)

title: EMI and repair service for assistive devices
problem: Only 29% of people with disabilities own assistive devices, and 43.5% say cost is the biggest barrier.
solution: Instalment plans, refurbished devices and local repair for wheelchairs, hearing aids and prosthetics.

checks.demand: Many pay out of pocket for devices and repair.
checks.today: Go without or use a broken device.
checks.who: Low-income users of mobility or hearing devices.
checks.wedge: Refurbish and finance wheelchairs for one city.
checks.seen: Ask 15 users how they paid for their device.
checks.future: Ageing adds demand for assistive products.

evidence.title: Can you buy a prosthetic on EMI? Critical gaps in assistive technology access (The Week)

title: Rental agreement and deposit tracker for tenants
problem: Tenants lose deposits and homes in broker or owner disputes, and many rentals still run on oral or unregistered agreements.
solution: App that creates a clear agreement, records deposit and move-in photos, and explains the rules of each state.

checks.demand: Tenants report sudden eviction and lost deposits.
checks.today: Rely on a broker and a stamp paper.
checks.wedge: Agreement plus photo record for 100 tenants.
checks.seen: Ask 20 tenants about their last deposit.
checks.future: More states are adopting the Model Tenancy Act.

evidence.title: We lost ₹70,000 overnight: Gurgaon tenants allege eviction (Business Today)
Model Tenancy Act: what tenants and landlords must know in 2026 (Housiey)
